_meta.companion: data/telescopes/gemini.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows vista.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; gemini: title, telescope (machine-readable mirrors, pupil, foci; refs point to sourced params as 'gemini.<param>'), explorer_preset (the proposed web/tpresets.js entry), params, not_found, conflicts, notes.
_meta.rule: Each value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/gemini/ (files reused from earlier rounds are byte-identical copies, marked in the cite). derived = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values. figure_readoff = a value read off a saved figure or drawing (the caption or OCR text is checked). INFERRED = a choice no source states. NOT FOUND marks a gap. Nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.quote_normalization: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, multiplication sign (to x), division slash, tilde operator, approximately-equal sign, middle dot, plus-minus (to +/-), the ordinal sign used as a degree normalized; soft hyphens and no-break spaces normalized; whitespace collapsed; a quote also passes against the text with PDF line-end hyphenation removed or closed up, or with all whitespace removed; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces (which may sit on consecutive pages).
_meta.texts_checked: pdftotext -layout and -raw per page and across consecutive page pairs (PDF p. = page index of the saved PDF; the stated page is machine-checked); tesseract 5.5.1 OCR (300 dpi) for the PDFs without a text layer (GBAF1, GBAF2); HTML as tag-stripped text (tags to a space, tags removed) and raw source (UTF-8 or windows-1252); .docx as the text of word/document.xml; .zmx as text (UTF-16 or UTF-8); .py as is.

explorer_preset.name: Gemini 8.1 m
explorer_preset.primaryNote: A thin ULE meniscus 8.1 m across and 20 cm thick with a 1.2 m central hole: a hyperboloid with f = 14.40 m (f/1.8), shaped by 120 actuators. explorer_preset.pupilNote: The 7.9 m pupil set by the secondary, less the secondary's 168 mm central hole (1.30 m in the pupil), through which a periscope shows infrared instruments cold sky, and four 10 mm vanes in two pairs (read off a pupil image from the Gemini Planet Imager; the pattern's orientation on the sky is not published).

Central obstruction in the IR configuration: 0.164 (GNICI; 168/1023 = 0.1642 DERIVED) vs 0.1515 (GZMN inner clear radius 77.55 mm) vs 0.146 (P06: 1.18 m of 8.1 m) vs 0.181 (FIGURE READ-OFF, S14 Fig. 6, relative to the imaged pupil edge).
Spider count: four struts (N22; four vanes in S14 Fig. 6) vs "two spider vanes" (P06, a lab simulator that modeled one vane).
Plate scale: 1.610 arcsec/mm (GTEL) vs 1.611 (GSPEC, GICD) vs 1.60994 (DERIVED from 128.12 m) vs 1.61028 (GN model) and 1.61143 (GS model).
Focal ratio: f/16 quoted (GTEL, G96, GALT) vs 16.2177 on the 7.9 m pupil (DERIVED; f/16.0 holds for an 8.0 m pupil).
Distance from the science fold to a side-port focus: 1100 mm (GZMS) vs 1095 mm (DERIVED from GICD: 795 mm to the port land plus 300 mm).
notes: One telescope for two: Gemini North and Gemini South share the design (G96: "identical in design"); the explorer entry stands for both, as the Keck entry does for Keck I and II. The prescriptions differ slightly (GZMN, GZMS); the pupil measurement is Gemini South's (GPI).

Cassegrain only: all instruments mount on the ISS at the single f/16 focus, on the up-looking port or on a side port behind the 45-deg science fold (one more silver reflection). The adaptive optics systems sit on side ports and pass the f/16 beam on (GALT).

The infrared design: the undersized secondary is the stop (7.9 m pupil), the secondary's 168 mm hole and a sky periscope show the infrared instruments cold sky in place of the primary's hole, the vanes are 10 mm thin, and the mirrors are silver. With the optical baffle extended (2.003 m) the obstruction grows to eps 0.254 and the periscope is shuttered.
The explorer offers the optical-baffle configuration as a third focus (a side port with eps 0.2535); the instrument's wavelength range sets the baffle position (GTEL: two positions, IR and Optical).
The NIRI preset (data/imaging/niri_hawki.md) uses D = 7.9 m, eps 0.164 and F = 16.22, the same telescope values.
